candidates.attacker_control: The attacker controls the bytes of a bootstrap ZIP that the build downloads and extracts: the p2 bootstrap archive (default https://repo.diffplug.com/misc/goomph-p2-bootstrap/<version>/goomph-p2-bootstrap-<version>.zip, or a URL supplied via goomph_override_p2bootstrapUrl) and the PDE bootstrap archive when goomph_override_pdeBootstrapUrl is set. ZIP entry names and contents are fully attacker-chosen; OkHttp follows redirects by default and no hash or signature check is performed on the downloaded archive before ZipMisc.unzip runs. Path segments like `../../../` in an entry name are passed through unchanged, and `new File(destinationDir, entry.getName())` plus FileOutputStream resolves `..` at the OS level.
candidates.counterevidence_checked: (1) Both call sites subsequently treat the same archive as a code channel (JarFolderRunner/ JarFolderRunnerExternalJvm load jars from the extracted `plugins/` folder; PdeInstallation runs the extracted launcher), so an attacker who fully controls the ZIP could plausibly obtain code execution even without the traversal; the traversal remains a distinct, independently triggered file-write primitive (any file name, any content, not just `plugins/*.jar`) and is the standard Zip Slip defect, but this reduces the marginal severity in a scenario where the archive is already trusted to execute. (2) The default download origin is HTTPS (repo.diffplug.com, download.eclipse.org via the p2 director), so a network-only attacker cannot trivially tamper with the archive; a compromised origin, an overridden/mirrored URL (explicitly supported by the documented `override_p2bootstrapUrl` / `override_pdeBootstrapUrl` settings), an HTTP mirror, or local cache tampering is required. (3) I searched for existing mitigations and found none: no `getCanonical*`/`normalize()`/`..`/containment checks anywhere in the tree, no checksum/signature verification around FileMisc.download, and no archive-entry validation at either call site. (4) The shipped Main.java (vendored Eclipse launcher) has a similar entry-name-to-path pattern in `extractFromJAR` (Main.java:2278-2333), which was considered but not chosen; it is upstream Eclipse code and requires a malicious fragment jar inside the installed IDE.
candidates.impact: Arbitrary file write outside the intended extraction directory with attacker-controlled content, limited only by the build user's filesystem permissions: overwrite user configuration or shell/startup profiles, SSH authorized_keys, files inside other projects, or files that the build/IDE later loads or executes; this can lead to persistence and, in realistic follow-on scenarios, code execution on the developer/CI machine. It also allows tampering with the goomph cache state (e.g. the `installed` token and previously extracted bootstrap files) to subvert later builds. The write happens before the extracted bootstrap is used, and does not require the attacker to win a race.
candidates.prerequisites: (1) The build uses any goomph task that provisions the p2 or PDE bootstrapper (e.g. p2AsMaven, oomphIde, p2 director, PDE build tasks) so that install() downloads and extracts the archive. (2) The attacker can influence the archive that is downloaded — e.g. compromise of the download host, a mirror/Nexus/cache configured via the documented `goomph_override_p2bootstrapUrl` / `goomph_override_pdeBootstrapUrl` overrides (documentation explicitly encourages relocating this URL to an internal server), an HTTP endpoint (no scheme enforcement), or tampering with the cached ZIP in `~/.goomph/p2-bootstrap/<release>/goomph-p2-bootstrap.zip`. (3) The build user's filesystem permissions bound what can be overwritten. No authentication or special configuration inside goomph is required to reach the vulnerable extraction path.
candidates.root_cause: ZipMisc.unzip (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/ZipMisc.java:176-191) takes every entry name from the archive and does `File dest = new File(destinationDir, entry.getName())` (line 180), then creates parent directories and writes the stream to that path (lines 182-187). There is no canonical/real-path containment check, no rejection of `..` segments or of entries that resolve outside destinationDir, and no entry-name sanitization. The only callers are P2BootstrapInstallation.install (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/p2/P2BootstrapInstallation.java:99) and PdeInstallation.install (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/pde/PdeInstallation.java:186), which extract an archive that was just downloaded to the same parent directory from an overridable URL (FileMisc.download, src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/FileMisc.java:55-72) without any checksum/signature verification. The download source is configurable through the public static fields/project properties exposed by GoomphCacheLocations (override_p2bootstrapUrl / `goomph_override_p2bootstrapUrl`, override_pdeBootstrapUrl / `goomph_override_pdeBootstrapUrl`, src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/GoomphCacheLocations.java:113-155; applied via initFromProject), so an internal mirror or proxy/cache can serve the archive.
candidates.title: Zip Slip in ZipMisc.unzip: downloaded bootstrap archives can write arbitrary files outside the extraction directory
candidates.trace: P2BootstrapInstallation.ensureInstalled() -> install() -> FileMisc.download(url, target) writes the archive to `<GoomphCacheLocations.p2bootstrap()>/<release>/goomph-p2-bootstrap.zip` -> ZipMisc.unzip(target, target.getParentFile()) -> while ((entry = zipInput.getNextEntry()) != null) -> dest = new File(destinationDir, entry.getName()) -> FileMisc.mkdirs(dest.getParentFile()) + new FileOutputStream(dest) + copy(zipInput, output). An entry such as `../../../.ssh/authorized_keys` resolves the destination path outside `<...>/<release>/` and three levels above the release folder reaches the user's home directory, so the file is created/overwritten there with the archive's content. PdeInstallation.install() has the identical pattern when `override_pdeBootstrapUrl` is configured (PdeInstallation.java:186).
candidates.unverified: I did not execute any code, build, test, or exploit; the traversal is established from source reading only. I did not verify which goomph release/build configuration first reaches the unzip call in practice, whether any Gradle-level input filtering could constrain the downloaded archive, or whether an upstream fix commit exists. The exact preconditions for attacker control of the download source (host compromise vs. configured mirror) are plausible but not demonstrated at runtime.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Improper Limitation of a Pathname to a Restricted Directory ('Path Traversal') / Zip Slip (CWE-29)

coverage_summary: Reviewed the assigned tree through get_source_scope (145 model-visible files; 0 excluded by name/size/symlink filters; binary-like files unreadable) and get_relation_scope (P1 index: 143 files indexed / 121 Java parsed, 1615 symbols, 2627 edges, 3507 unresolved calls; 2 source files missing from the index; index capabilities are syntax-only — no control-flow, data-flow, semantic resolution, or runtime verification). I listed all files and read the security-relevant majority in full or in part: ZipMisc, FileMisc, CmdLine, SerializableMisc, JavaExecable(+Imp), JavaExecWinFriendly, JRE, Lazyable, NativeFileManager, ProjectPlugin, GoomphCacheLocations, ConfigMisc, ProjectPlugin/StateBuilder, MavenCentralMapping/Extension/Plugin, p2 (P2Model, P2BootstrapInstallation, P2AntRunner, P2Declarative, AsMaven*, MavenRepoBuilder, ParsedJar, FeaturesAndBundlesPublisher, CategoryPublisher), pde (PdeInstallation, PdeBuildTask, PdeAntBuildTask, PdeBuildProperties, PdeProductBuildConfig, ProductFileUtil, PluginCatalog, CopyJarsUsingProductFile, EclipseRelease, ExplicitVersionPolicy, JdkConfig), eclipserunner (EclipseApp, EclipseIni, EclipseIniLauncher, EclipseFont? runner classes, EquinoxLauncher/Launch*, JarFolderRunner*, NativeRunner, JRE), oomph (OomphIdeExtension/Plugin, Setup*, WorkspaceRegistry, BrandingProductPlugin, InstalledJre*, Convention*, EclipseMisc, IUs, thirdparty), osgi (BndManifest*, OsgiExec*), swt, and the vendored launcher (Main.java partially, 2808 lines; JNIBridge, Constants, package-info). I also inspected build/config/docs (build.gradle, gradle.properties, settings.gradle, CHANGES.md, README, CICD config, wrapper properties, resources). I did not read every line of the 2808-line vendored Eclipse launcher or of every apt/console-plugin wrapper class, and the snapshot contains no tests, so nothing was executed or runtime-confirmed.
limitations: No code execution, build, test, scanner, or exploit was run; all findings are static source-reading leads, not runtime-confirmed vulnerabilities.

The P1 relation index is syntactic/navigation-only: control flow, data flow, semantic resolution, reachability and Spring/runtime behavior are not implemented, and 3507 call edges are unresolved; 2 source files are missing from the index, so absence of an index record for a code area does not mean it was reviewed there.
No tests exist in the snapshot (the repository's src/test tree is absent), so no regression test could be used to confirm intent or behavior.
Dependency-level vulnerabilities (e.g. okhttp 4.3.1, commons-io 2.6, bndlib 6.1.0, Gradle 6.8.2 wrapper) were not evaluated against CVE databases and are outside the source-level scope.
Attacker-control prerequisites for the ZIP Slip candidate (compromise/mirroring of the bootstrap download URL, cache tampering) are reasoned from source and documentation but not demonstrated.
The 2,808-line vendored Eclipse launcher (Main.java) and some small plugin/wrapper classes were reviewed selectively rather than line-by-line.

rejected_leads.lead: XXE: MavenCentralMapping.parse (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/eclipse/MavenCentralMapping.java:79-99) uses a default DocumentBuilderFactory and parses artifacts.xml streamed from the downloaded artifacts.jar (parseFromFile, lines 155-161; download at line 150) with no disallow-doctype-decl / external-entity restrictions. Attacker-controlled XML from a configured update site could trigger local file disclosure or SSRF during configuration.
rejected_leads.reason: Rejected in favor of the ZIP Slip only as the single strongest issue: the update site is normally download.eclipse.org over HTTPS, the XML is a data-only channel, impact (file read/DoS) is lower and exfiltration is awkward (parsed values become dependency versions), and a missing parser hardening flag is closer to a hardening gap unless a malicious update site is clearly in scope. Not fixed/confirmed at runtime.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal from unvalidated OSGi Bundle-SymbolicName: MavenRepoBuilder.close (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/p2/MavenRepoBuilder.java:57-64, artifacts installed at 50-54 and 88-100) and EquinoxLaunchSetupTask.copyFiles (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/EquinoxLaunchSetupTask.java:53-57) use parsed jar manifest values as path segments when writing files under the p2asmaven output or the launch directory (ParsedJar.getSymbolicName, ParsedJar.java:62-94, performs no character validation).
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible CWE-22, but the output file names are constrained (`<artifactId>-<version>[-sources].jar`) and the same jars become build dependencies (code channel), so it is a weaker/duplicative variant of the same file-write class; not chosen as the single candidate.

rejected_leads.lead: Command injection via NativeRunner: run() (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/NativeRunner.java:37-49) concatenates the launcher plus all arguments into one string that CmdLine.runCmd executes through `/bin/sh -c` or `cmd /c` (CmdLine.java:138-205), while FileMisc.quote (FileMisc.java:157-168) only adds double quotes when the value contains a space and never escapes quotes/`;`/`$()`/backticks.
rejected_leads.reason: The values reaching these arguments come from the invoking build configuration (p2 repository URLs, IU ids, `-D` properties, workspace/builder paths), not from remote artifacts; no demonstrated remote attacker-controlled flow into this sink. Rejected as an unconfirmed lead.

rejected_leads.lead: Unsafe deserialization: SerializableMisc.read (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/SerializableMisc.java:39-45) calls ObjectInputStream.readObject() with no class filtering, used on temp files created by JavaExecable/OsgiExecable (JavaExecableImp.java:39-57, OsgiExecable.java:81-88, OsgiExecImp.java:69-73) and on the path passed to JavaExecable.main (JavaExecable.java:165-178).
rejected_leads.reason: The serialized data is produced and consumed by the same build (File.createTempFile paths), so only a local attacker with the ability to replace the temp file could exploit it; no remote source found. Rejected as low-severity/local-only for this review.

rejected_leads.lead: WorkspaceRegistry cleanup deletes owner-less subdirectories under GoomphCacheLocations.workspaces() (WorkspaceRegistry.java:80-93, 113-137), whose root can be redirected via project properties/static overrides (GoomphCacheLocations.initFromProject, lines 54-61; override_workspaces).
rejected_leads.reason: Triggering it requires control of the build's own project properties/configuration, i.e. inputs already as trusted as the build script (which is code); no remote artifact can set these. Rejected as outside the reachable remote threat model.

rejected_leads.lead: Path traversal in the vendored Eclipse launcher: Main.extractFromJAR (src/main/java/com/diffplug/gradle/eclipserunner/launcher/Main.java:2278-2333) builds the extraction path from a jar entry name (entry must start with `eclipse_`) and later JNIBridge loads the extracted library (JNIBridge.java:60-83; chmod at Main.java:545-553).
rejected_leads.reason: The file is a documented copy of upstream Eclipse Equinox launcher code (header at Main.java:50-60) and exploitation requires a malicious fragment jar inside the installed IDE/p2 mirror; the entry-name traversal angle overlaps with the chosen candidate but is in vendored code and not selected.

summary: goomph (Gradle plugins for Eclipse/OSGi tooling) was reviewed as a defensive source assessment. The snapshot contains 145 model-visible files (121 Java); there are no tests in the snapshot, so no runtime validation was possible. The strongest source-evidenced issue is a Zip Slip (CWE-22/CWE-29) in the shared archive-extraction helper: ZipMisc.unzip builds extraction paths directly from archive entry names with no containment or `..` validation, and both call sites feed it bootstrap ZIPs that the build downloads from a configurable, unverified URL and then extracts into the per-user `~/.goomph` cache. A crafted archive entry such as `../../../<sensitive file>` escapes the intended destination (three levels up from `~/.goomph/p2-bootstrap/<release>/` reaches the user's home directory) and is written with attacker-chosen content and permissions allowed by the OS. Alternatives were examined and are recorded as rejected leads, most notably an unhardened DocumentBuilderFactory XML parse of remote `artifacts.xml` (XXE) and path construction from unvalidated OSGi Bundle-SymbolicName values. No exploitation, code execution, or tests were performed.
